plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double flowers above deep green, glossy divided foliage. A beloved cottage garden staple and cut flower, it thrives in cold winters and can persist for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia, and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peony plants can live for over 100 years, and ants are often seen on the flower buds feeding on sugary nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest cultivated roses, this compact, suckering shrub produces fragrant, semi-double flowers with golden stamens. It is hardy and was ancestral to many modern garden roses.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (June in Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to central and southern Europe and western Asia; cultivated in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Dried petals of Rosa gallica 'Officinalis' were used in medieval apothecaries and retain their fragrance long after drying, earning it the name Apothecary's Rose.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like foliage and large clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers that cover the canopy and carpet the ground beneath. In Northern Hemisphere subtropics, bloom begins in late spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); September to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Mexico, southern California, Florida, South Africa, and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas line the streets that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, and in some places falling blossoms are said to bring good luck.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: A rugged Australian tree or shrub with thick, serrated leaves and large cylindrical flower spikes made of thousands of tiny individual flowers. It is an important nectar source for birds and mammals in the cooler months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly February to August, with peak flowering around early winter)
plants.location: Eastern coast of Australia, from Queensland to Victoria and Tasmania
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones are woody and often open only after bushfire, releasing seeds into the ash-enriched soil.
